design.md's own ## Security Boundaries names the fail-closed input boundaries, the no-new-write-surface boundary, and the protected-file/human-copy boundary. security-spec.md (normative refinement) extends this with a full Trust Boundaries section, a STRIDE table (B1-B6) naming mechanism at each boundary, a Data Classification table explicitly stating no PII/credential is handled by any entity, and an OWASP Mapping table. B5's STRIDE row and Security Tests row were extended in this round to name design.md's contract point 5's five properties individually (per-target atomic publish with in-step digest verification; explicit no-transaction/no-rollback acknowledgment; live-state reporting on any post-copy-phase failure, enumerating installed/failed/not-attempted and stating installed files are live and not rolled back; recovery by re-running with an already-correct target as a no-op; and the pre-copy-phase failure branch reporting that no live file was modified) rather than referring to the point collectively -- this closes round 2's Major finding. The human-copy runner script itself (apply-protected-files.ps1) is not in this reviewer's manifest, so the extended rows are judged on internal consistency with design.md's own point 5 text rather than against the runner's actual code; on that basis the extended text matches design.md point-5 language closely and does not claim any property design.md does not itself state.
